note: Companies with material local-market revenue exposure in high-eta categories (health eta=1.26, recreation=1.31, restaurants/services=1.28, durables=1.15). Revenue figures are [OBS] where taken from company reports or cited analyst sources; marked [INF] where estimated or second-hand.

companies.name: Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd
companies.revenue_note: India's largest private hospital chain; 9,463 operational beds. Healthcare services 50% of revenue; pharmacy/digital 42%. FY25 revenue figure not stated but mkt cap ~$15B USD.
companies.revenue_cagr_note: 3-year revenue CAGR behind Max and Fortis per comparison source.
companies.provenance: [OBS] univest.in citing NSE data as of 19 Aug 2026; YouTube video transcript Q1 FY26

companies.name: Fortis Healthcare Ltd
companies.provenance: [OBS] in.investing.com; Fortis Q1FY27 earnings release Aug 2026

pairs.refutation_factor: India's public health spending expansion (Ayushman Bharat, government hospital capacity) could cap private hospital demand growth among lower-income households who are the Engel transition cohort.
pairs.note: India food share 28.3% (national accounts) vs 43% rural households (HCES survey) — the transition cohort is rural/semi-urban where private hospital access is limited. The Engel mechanism is real but the addressable cohort for listed private hospitals may be the urban-middle, not the Engel-crossing rural population.

companies.name: Mobile World Investment Corporation (The Gioi Di Dong)
companies.local_exposure_pct: ~95%+ Vietnam (3 retail chains: TGDD phones, DMX electronics, BHX grocery)
companies.provenance: [OBS] Shinhan Securities Vietnam Update Report Jul 2026; theinvestor.vn H1 2026; investing.com
companies.note: 2023 revenue dip to 118T from 133T reflects post-COVID normalisation of phone demand. Recovery in 2024-25 driven by electronics + grocery (BHX). MWG's grocery chain (BHX) captures a different Engel thesis: as food share falls, Vietnamese households shift from wet markets to modern retail.

companies.name: FPT Corporation
companies.local_exposure_pct: ~50% Vietnam; 50% international IT services (30+ countries, 100+ Fortune 500 clients)
companies.note: FPT is primarily an IT services exporter, not a domestic-Engel play. The Vietnam household digital consumption channel is BHX/MWG, not FPT. FPT is noted as a Vietnam growth stock but its Engel linkage is indirect (rising incomes → more IT talent demand from global clients).

pairs.refutation_factor: Vietnam's consumer electronics market is heavily import-dependent; MWG's revenue reflects retail margins on products that are manufactured in China/Korea. If exchange rates or import costs rise, MWG's margins compress without a household income effect.
pairs.note: Durables elasticity in OECD (1.15) likely understates the Vietnam transition effect, where consumer electronics penetration was low and is rising fast. But COICOP share data is a GAP — the Engel mechanism is plausible but not yet measured.

companies.name: Siloam International Hospitals Tbk
companies.note: Indonesia's largest hospital chain (Lippo Group). Listed IDX.

companies.name: Mitra Keluarga Karyasehat Tbk
companies.note: Premium Jakarta-area hospital network; 90% private patients. EBITDA margin 38% significantly higher than Siloam (22%) — targets higher-income cohort that is already post-transition.

pairs.refutation_factor: Indonesia's BPJS Kesehatan (national health insurance, ~95% population coverage) competes directly with private hospitals for routine care. If government reimbursement expands, the Engel-driven private hospital growth depends on premium/complex care differentiation, not volume.
pairs.note: Indonesia health COICOP share is a GAP. The Engel mechanism requires that rising incomes shift out-of-pocket health spending to private facilities — this is plausible given low public hospital quality but not yet measured in annual time-series.

companies.name: Cleopatra Hospitals Group S.A.E.
companies.provenance: [OBS] in.investing.com; Forbes Middle East 2022 ($454M mkt cap, $137M sales, $22M profit at 2022 prices)
companies.note: Egypt's leading private hospital consolidator (6 hospitals, 789 beds as of 2022). Revenue USD $137M in 2022 (Forbes). Listed EGX 2016. Relevant caveat: Egypt's 2022-23 inflation (+40% food prices, EGP devaluation) made food share rise; against-grain mover. Rising medical costs may suppress volume even if incomes rise nominally.

pairs.refutation_factor: Egypt's EGP devaluation (2022-2023: ~50%) creates a dual problem: nominal incomes rise but real purchasing power falls; AND medical equipment/drug imports become more expensive, raising hospital costs faster than revenues. The Engel mechanism is overwhelmed by the macro shock.
pairs.note: Egypt is in the upper half of the transition zone (37% predicted food share, ~60% probability of exiting by 2027). But 2017-2023 food share ROSE +3.3pp — the inflation story dominates. Egypt is included for completeness but is the WEAKEST Engel-to-healthcare chain of the four.

companies.name: MTN Nigeria Communications Plc
companies.note: Nigeria's largest telecom by market cap ($12.6B USD). Mobile data and financial services (MTN MoMo) are the Engel-adjacent play: as Nigerians cannot yet afford most discretionary goods, data access and mobile money are the first non-food priority. H1-2026 profit after tax +70.6% despite macroeconomic headwinds — driven by subscriber growth and ARPU expansion as data penetration deepens.
companies.provenance: [OBS] tradingeconomics.com citing NGX; businessinsider.africa article; YouTube transcript H1-2026 earnings
companies.refutation_specific: MTN Nigeria's revenue is partly driven by higher prices (inflation pass-through) not volume — if the naira stabilises and competition intensifies, ARPU growth may not persist even with Engel-driven data demand.

companies.name: Dangote Cement Plc
companies.note: Urbanisation is the Engel proxy for Nigeria: as income rises even modestly, households upgrade from mud/informal housing to cement-block construction. Dangote Cement captures this. Revenue growth driven by volume (double-digit pan-Africa) and price. This is a durables/housing play (η≈1.15 in OECD), not communication, but may be the cleaner Engel mechanism in Nigeria because it is less inflation-distorted.
companies.provenance: [OBS] Forbes Africa 2024; NGX market cap data; tradingeconomics.com
companies.refutation_specific: Cement demand also depends on government infrastructure spending; a fiscal consolidation that cuts public construction would compress volumes independently of household income.

pairs.refutation_factor: Nigeria's flat food share 2017-2023 despite GDP within the break CI is the primary falsifier: if the Engel mechanism requires income growth to reach households — rather than being concentrated at the top — the listed-company plays require broad-based income growth that has not materialised yet. Naira devaluation compresses real incomes faster than GDP PPP growth suggests.
pairs.note: Nigeria presents the African Engel paradox: the GDP suggests transition, the food share says no. Listed companies MTN and Dangote are plays on urbanisation and data penetration, which are arguably the *precursors* to the Engel transition, not the transition itself. Appropriate as a 'watch' market rather than an active Engel play.

companies.name: Netcare Ltd
companies.note: South Africa's largest private hospital group. With food share already at 21.3%, the post-transition South African household is spending on health. Netcare is the private healthcare infrastructure. The Engel story here is POST-transition: health share rising as food share has already fallen. Differently from India, South Africa's private healthcare serves the formal-sector employed middle class, not a transitioning subsistence population.
companies.provenance: [INF] market cap estimate from analyst range; JSE listing confirmed
companies.refutation_specific: National Health Insurance (NHI) bill, if implemented, could restructure private healthcare financing and compress private hospital pricing power.

companies.name: Shoprite Holdings Ltd
companies.note: Africa's largest food retailer. The Engel play: as food's share falls (21.3% in ZAF), the remaining food spending formalises — from local markets and spazas toward supermarket chains. Shoprite also operates in Nigeria, Kenya, and other transition markets, giving it the multi-stage Engel exposure across the continent.
companies.provenance: [OBS] JSE listing; known from prior session analysis

pairs.refutation_factor: South Africa's GDP growth has been near zero (ZAF GDP growth projected 0% in 2030 path), so the 'freed budget' story depends on slow-moving demographic shifts rather than income growth. The transition is complete but the income base is stagnating.
pairs.note: South Africa is the most developed market in sub-Saharan Africa but also the most stagnant in income growth. The Engel thesis applies to premiumisation and formalisation of spending rather than the initial transition.

companies.name: Safaricom PLC
companies.note: M-PESA is the most direct Engel-transition instrument in Africa: as Kenyan households cross the food threshold, the first non-food priority is mobile money (bill payment, savings, credit) rather than formal banking. M-PESA now has 35.82M active customers in Kenya and 42.2% of service revenue. The communication category has η=0.79 in OECD, but in Kenya where formal banking penetration was ~30% at M-PESA's launch, mobile money functions as a financial-inclusion luxury with effective elasticity >> 1. FY2026 group service revenue crossed KES 400B for the first time (10.8% growth); Kenya profit after tax KES 94.95B.
companies.provenance: [OBS] Safaricom Annual Report FY24; Mwango Capital FY26 analysis; LinkedIn M-PESA Africa post FY25 results

pairs.refutation_factor: The 2023 food-share drop (42.1% from 56.6%) is a single data point that may reflect post-pandemic recomposition rather than genuine Engel transition. If the 2024/25 USDA data shows reversion to ~55%, the Kenya transition story weakens. Additionally, Safaricom's Ethiopia operations are deeply loss-making and dilute the group's returns from the Kenya Engel story.
pairs.note: Kenya is the most plausible new-entry Engel market in Africa for 2024-2030. The 2023 food-share data point needs verification — but if confirmed, Safaricom is positioned to capture the financial-inclusion dimension of the transition before any other African company. The communication category may understate Safaricom's effective elasticity because M-PESA is simultaneously communication, financial services, and infrastructure.

companies.name: Fomento Económico Mexicano (FEMSA)
companies.local_exposure_pct: ~70% Mexico; 30% rest of LatAm (Colombia, Chile, Peru, Brazil, European Valora)
companies.note: FEMSA is the most direct Engel-transition investment in Mexico and possibly in all of Latin America. As Mexico's food share has fallen from ~35% to 25.7%, the freed budget goes two places that FEMSA captures simultaneously: (1) OXXO convenience (restaurants/services η=1.28): Mexicans formalise snack and prepared-food spending from street vendors to OXXO — 24,000 stores, one on every corner, billing payment + food + coffee + financial services; (2) Health Division (pharmacies YZA, Moderna, Cruz Verde — health η=1.26): as incomes rise, out-of-pocket pharma and wellness spending increases. FEMSA Health grew 10.5% in FY2025. FEMSA is also expanding OXXO in Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Chile — giving multi-country Engel-transition exposure in one vehicle. SPIN fintech (9.4M active users, +18.8% in 2Q25) is the M-PESA equivalent embedded in OXXO stores.
companies.provenance: [OBS] koalagains.com business analysis FY2025; cspdailynews.com Q2 2026 earnings; femsa.com press release; Reuters Q1 revenue report

companies.name: Walmart de México y Centroamérica (Walmex)
companies.note: Walmart Mexico captures the formalisation of food and consumer discretionary spending in post-transition Mexico. As food share falls from 25.7% toward 20%, Mexican households shift from tianguis (informal markets) to Sam's Club and Walmart supercenters. Walmex is also building a fintech layer (Bait telecom, Cashi wallet, credits). Consumer recovery has been slow in 2025-26 ('tepid consumer spending'), giving a cautious short-term view but the long-run Engel story remains intact. Caveat: Walmex's growth is partly ticket-size inflation, not volume, at the current cycle.
companies.provenance: [OBS] mexicobusiness.news Q2 2026; Walmex 2Q26 Earnings Release PDF; Yahoo Finance Q2 2025

pairs.refutation_factor: Mexico's consumer spending recovery has been slower than expected in 2025-26, with WALMEX noting 'tepid consumption' and transaction declines. The Engel mechanism is structural but the timing depends on real income growth, which may lag behind the food-share trend given peso depreciation and uncertainty. Additionally, FEMSA's non-Mexico operations (Valora Europe) could dilute the Engel thesis if European operations underperform.
pairs.note: Mexico is the cleanest post-transition Latin American Engel play. Food at 25.7% (USDA) or 32.1% (model), with 130 million people and a large formal retail sector already in place. FEMSA uniquely combines restaurants/services (η=1.28), health (η=1.26), and fintech (first non-food wallet for many Mexicans) in one listed vehicle — making it arguably the most multi-dimensional Engel company in the entire analysis.

companies.name: Yduqs Participações S.A. (formerly Estácio)
companies.note: Yduqs (Estácio, Ibmec, IDOMED brands) is the clearest post-transition Engel play in Brazil and arguably in all of Latin America. The thesis: Brazil crossed the 35% food threshold years ago; the first generation of families where nobody went to university is now entering the workforce and sending children to private higher education. Education has η=0.974 in the OECD (near unity), but in Brazil where public university access is highly competitive, private higher education is effectively a luxury (η>1) for the emerging middle class. FCF R$1.051B in 2025 (+32% YoY); student intake +14% Q3-2025. Market cap R$3.58B vs FCF R$1B = very cheap if growth continues. The Milei-Lula uncertainty and Brazil's slow economic growth are the risks.
companies.provenance: [OBS] yduqs.com.br IR press release March 2026 (FY2025 results); finzer.io market cap Oct 2026

companies.name: Rede D'Or São Luiz S.A.
companies.note: Brazil's largest private hospital group ($8.9B USD revenue). Health η=1.26 in OECD; in post-transition Brazil, with food share at 16.2%, health spending is one of the fastest-growing non-food categories. Rede D'Or's thesis: as Brazilian middle class deepens, complex care (oncology +22.3% YoY), elective surgery, and premium insurance (SulAmérica subsidiary) grow faster than routine care. Q2-2026: missed EPS estimate but EBITDA +18.2% — margin expansion story is intact.
companies.provenance: [OBS] investing.com RDOR3 page; zoominfo.com revenue; Reuters/Yahoo Finance Q2-2026 results

pairs.refutation_factor: Brazil's slow GDP growth (~2-3% real) means the Engel-driven market expansion is gradual. For Yduqs specifically, the federal government's PROUNI/FIES student finance programs (which subsidise private education) have been volatile — any policy reversal compresses enrollment. For Rede D'Or, Brazil's SUS (public health system) competes for routine care; the private market depends on premium insurance penetration growing faster than overall income.
pairs.note: Brazil is the richest Engel case in Latin America because it has BOTH the data (POF 2017-18 with education at 4.7%) AND the listed companies to test the thesis. Education and health are the two luxury categories (η>1 in the OECD sense) most clearly at play in a post-transition economy where food is already below 20%. Brazil's B3 is the most liquid market in Latin America.

companies.name: Grupo Financiero Galicia (via Ggal/GGAL ADR)
companies.note: In hyperinflationary Argentina, the Engel mechanism works differently: the category with the fastest-growing budget share is not food (which is expensive) but financial services — as Argentines desperately seek dollar savings, credit cards, and inflation hedges. Grupo Galicia is the leading private bank. The Engel lens here is inverted: financial services (η≈1.37) capture spending precisely because food prices are out of control, not because food share has fallen peacefully. This is the 'Argentina paradox': post-transition GDP but pre-transition consumer behaviour.
companies.provenance: [INF] BYMA listing confirmed; thesis constructed from macro context

pairs.refutation_factor: Argentina's entire macroeconomic situation is a refutation of the standard Engel thesis. Real incomes fell sharply in 2022-2023 despite nominal GDP PPP appearing high. The Milei administration's shock therapy (2024+) may restore stability but the near-term outlook for consumer spending is highly uncertain. Argentina is included for analytical completeness but is NOT recommended as an Engel-investment candidate without resolution of the macro situation.
pairs.note: Argentina is the clearest case where the Engel mechanism is overwhelmed by macro factors. GDP PPP of $27,847 suggests deep post-transition, but chronic 100%+ inflation means the population is actually in survival mode for budget allocation. FULL COICOP data is a GAP (no ENGHo since 2017-18). The only Engel-adjacent investment thesis is financial formalisation, which is happening but driven by inflation-hedging demand rather than income growth. Argentina is a 'watch' market, not an active Phase 3 candidate.
